Voynich MS - Quire 5

General

For an explanation of the material found on this page, see here.

Description

Quire 5 is a standard quire containing folios 33 through 40. The gathering mark is on f40v.

Schematic folio layout:

Folio 33

Normal folio. The folio nr. is on f33r.

f33r  

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.
It has the folio nr. (33) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

Plant with green flowers and faces drawn in the roots.

This plant shows some similarity with plant fragment #31 on f89r1.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
(none)

Text

This page has 7 text items (loci), as follows:
7 lines of standard text in paragraphs.

There are seven lines of text in a single paragraph.

Currier language: B
RZ language: C (page) / C (folio) / C (bifolio)
LFD hand: 2

Browse interlinear transliteration of f33r

Tentative identifications

ELV: mandragora?

Other information

Similar heads in roots are found in the alchemical herbals. Alternatively, the heads in the roots could be a reference to to 'testes' and thus to an orchid, though the plant does not look like one.

  f33v

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Illustration(s)

Plant with 2 huge flowers on top, and a third (dead) one hanging down behind one of the leaves. Starry (fingered) leaves and roots that look like sea mines.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
(none)

Text

This page has 11 text items (loci), as follows:
11 lines of standard text in paragraphs.

There are 11 lines of text in two paragraphs, which avoid parts of the drawing.

Currier language: B
RZ language: C- (page) / C (folio) / C (bifolio)
LFD hand: 2

Browse interlinear transliteration of f33v

Tentative identifications

ELV: knautia, scabiosa. ThP: scabiosa.

Other information

This page is occasionally mistaken to be the sunflower that O'Neill described in his 1944 publication. However, O'Neill was referring to f93r instead.

This page is discussed extensively at >> one of Jorge Stolfi's web pages. Illustrations of this page figured in numerous publications.

Normal folio. The folio nr. is on f34r. The parchment has a hole in the lower half.

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.
There is a hole in the parchment which has been integrated in the drawing.
It has the folio nr. (34) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

Drawing of a plant with large roots, leaves ending in 'figers' and three flowers.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):

β: leaves parallel and fused together on one stalk

Text

This page has 15 text items (loci), as follows:
15 lines of standard text in paragraphs.

There are 16 lines of text in three paragraphs. All text is split by the plant and in the second paragraph the lines left and right are not aligned very well. This seems to end in a 'signature'.

Currier language: B
RZ language: Bs (page) / B (folio) / B (bifolio)
LFD hand: 2

Browse interlinear transliteration of f34r

Tentative identifications

ELV: scabiosa. ThP: scabiosa.

Other information

Nick Pelling suggests that the hole in the parchment was created deliberately by the author/artist.

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Illustration(s)

Plant that looks like a tree with a straight stem (trunk) and strong roots. Oak leaves at the top and sides, and braches with currants twining around it.

This plant shows some similarity with plant fragment #35 on f89r2.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
α: two or more leaf clusters/clumps
α: berries that have no added circles

Text

This page has 21 text items (loci), as follows:
21 lines of standard text in paragraphs.

The text is in a single paragraph. All lines short, left of the drawing.

Currier language: A
RZ language: A (page) / A (folio) / A (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f35v

Tentative identifications

This is similar to drawings of ivy twining an oak tree in several manuscripts of the Tractatus de Herbis tradition.

ELV: uva quercina, the fabulous 'grapes of oak'. ThP: uva quercina, oak quercus gall apple? No! grapevine?

Other information
